terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A body-on-frame seven-seat SUV. The plate shows a very dark (black-plum) wagon body with chrome window surrounds and pillar covers, ten-spoke alloy wheels under wide black arch flares, aluminium side steps, black roof rails on a ribbed roof, a spare-wheel bulge on the hatch and warm dust on the lower doors and the whole rear. NOTE for the asset list: the plate's badge is a three-diamond mark and the body is a Pajero-type SUV, not a Fortuner; the model is built to the plate, which is the authority, and the discrepancy is a preview-image problem. Reclassified large -> hero on 2026-09-02 (same envelope class as the four hero pickups and vans; 4,000 triangles could not carry spoked wheels).

reasoning: The identity is the side profile -- bonnet, raked screen, long wagon roof and a near-vertical hatch -- and it is one closed polygon swept across the width, with the wheel arches cut into it as notches, then narrowed above the belt for tumblehome. One geometry carries the whole shell.
One repetition system: four wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.
A colour difference is not a material difference: every trim tone -- tyre, rim, bumper, lamp -- is a vertex colour on one white material, and the paint carries its dirt as a canvas.
Action readiness is the wheels: four hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A vehicle cannot be a box on a box: the raked screen, the tumblehome and the arches are what make it read at prop distance, and all three come from shaping one extrusion. The glasshouse is a second extrusion of the cab polygon offset 6 mm proud so no pane shares a plane with the body. The roof carries two black rails and five ribs, the hatch a spare-wheel bulge, a chrome garnish and a glass pane on its rake.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The front elevation is built to type: a two-bar chrome grille between rectangular lamps over a grey bumper.

The paint is HELD DARK on chroma, not lifted: the plate's door-upper measures #252427 (luma 36, sat 0.08) and two earlier builds lifted it to #5a5a5e because a neutral flank rendering near the backdrop's luma 58 read as a hole. The third build authors a black-plum #2b2339 at sat 0.39, which renders at luma ~32 on the flank and stays chromatic on the key-lit roof, and the turntable gate passes at all four azimuths with the largest enclosed component 313 px (the wheel well behind the spokes).
Mirrors reach 1.04 m either side of centre; the registry width of 1.86 is the body width.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.86 x 1.84 x 4.80 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=6 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (4); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

The Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.404 : 0.448 (2.47 lengths tall against the declared 2.61), so heights are proxy fractions of H and stations fractions of L at the declared metres.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/side.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: sills, lower doors, rear body and arches
localOverrides.evidence: Lower-door and rear dust against the flank; a zoned wash to 0.36 of a 2 m height-keyed tile plus streaks and speckle at the envelope.

evidence: Clean paint measured on viewEvidence region-side (PBR confidence 0.860) at #252427 / #3f3e3a (door upper and lower, luma 36-62) and on the tailgate at #413f40. Authored CLEAN #2b2339 (luma 40, sat 0.39): the plate's hue with enough chroma that the turntable gate keeps the shaded flank as foreground where two neutral builds were read as holes. The dust film on the lower doors and rear (plate #373533 over black) is authored as a warm #564c40, brighter than the paint in every channel, so the material carries the dust as its envelope and the clean paint rides the canvas as ratio(#2b2339, #564c40) formed in linear space.

Textureless as DECLARED: the dust is a 512 px Canvas 2D mud tile bound after construction as map -- zoned behind the front wheel, over the whole rear body and ahead of the rear arch, solid to 0.22 of a 2 m height-keyed tile, 200 spray streaks, 3000 speckles, upward faces keyed into the clean band.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: three components and one InstancedMesh at 4 draw calls of 6, costed before geometry existed.
Roof rails and panel floated 2.5-5 cm above the roof; the gate read the daylight under them as a 567 x 12 px hole on both flanks. Seated on the roof.

Owner review (v4, 2026-09-03): "the hood is very boxy". The shoulder fillet stopped at the rake top, so the bonnet's side edges were square creases. A second r 0.10 shoulder now runs the bonnet edges (in over z 1.42-1.52 so the A strip's foot is untouched, out over 2.00-2.20 ahead of the nose rounding), and the shell sweeps 14 columns at edgeBias 0.5 -- 10 at 0.6 put ONE vertex on each fillet arc, a 12 x 10 cm chamfer. 5,752 -> 6,292 triangles.

Owner review (v4): "the lights and the bumper are very boxy". The bumper and slot corners were one 36 cm box at 0.62 rad, a chord with a step at each end, and the lamps 3 cm slabs standing 6-9 cm off the bonnet-lip arc. Bumper and slot corners are now five and four 20-degree chords of the nose arc (cfg `chord()`), the lamps a flat inner unit plus a 40-degree chord, tilted back 26 degrees with the lip arc and 2 cm proud.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 5,752/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two canvases (512 px mud, 256 px glass) at 1.7 MB, factory ~110 ms. Reclassified large -> hero for the spoked wheels. Colliders re-derived at the 0.025 voxel: 8 boxes, coverage 0.948.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: 3 components and one repetition system: 4 of 6. The pillars ride the shell; every trim part rides one merge.

materials.note: paint, glass and a white vertex-coloured trim: 3 of 4. Tyres, rims, bumpers and lamps differ in albedo only.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 5,752 of 8,000: one extrusion with two 8-segment arches, a 20-segment wheel lathe, and boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A closed side-profile polygon extruded across the width and shaped per vertex (tumblehome above the belt, plan rounding at nose and tail); an offset extrusion of the cabin polygon for the glass; a lathe for the wheel; boxes for everything else.
One InstancedMesh carries the four wheels; the right-side instances are yawed a half turn so the dish faces out. No per-instance colour, so the white base is inert.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. TWO post-construction Canvas 2D tiles: a 512 px zoned mud tile as the paint map and a 256 px sky-gradient glass tile as the glazing map, both ratios formed in linear space. 1.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory ~110 ms.
